plain: The quality of being able to change

webster.text: Changeableness; susceptibility of change; the quality of being subject to change or alteration, either in form, state or essential qualities.

more.text: Changeableness, as of mind, disposition or will; inconstancy; instability; as the mutability of opinion or purpose.

example.quote: The mutability in the public councils arising from a rapid succession of new members, however qualified they may be, points out, in the strongest manner, the necessity of some stable institution in the government.
